gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Contemporary and geometric, Redux spaces its letters wide. Noto Sans Nushu follows with a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke, so the two fill a page with generous, upright lines.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Clean lines and wide spacing mark Redux, whose curves swing in with a big visible entrance. Noto Sans Ogham brings tall bodies that look bold and wide gaps in the e, so making the heading small wastes what Redux does well.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Noto Sans Ol Chiki keeps its curve tails well back from the body. Next to Redux, whose crossbars run a touch thinner than its stems, it makes words look like solid blocks instead of skylines.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-old-hungar: Redux is the display voice here, with wide spacing and a visible entrance into every curve. Noto Sans Old Hungarian handles the quieter job, keeping its large counters in tall a, e and s open even at tiny sizes.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Barely any gap separates x-height from cap height in Noto Sans Old Italic, and its curve endings stay well apart. Redux does the showy work with subdued contrast and wide spacing; this one just reads.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-old-north-: Redux spreads wide, geometric letters with horizontals a notch lighter than the uprights. Noto Sans Old North Arabian sits beneath it as a dense, tall lowercase band, its terminals pointing outward like a pair of tongs.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-old-persia: A faint nib-pressure wobble runs through each round letter of Redux, and its wide spacing stays open. And Noto Sans Old Persian offers lofty, tall lowercase with counters that breathe, leaving Redux to earn its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdia: Redux enters each curve with a big visible swoop, its lowercase enlarged and its modulation light. Noto Sans Old Sogdian answers with an x-height nearly touching cap height, wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Redux shows a faint weight difference between its upstrokes and downstrokes. Its wide spacing meets Noto Sans Old Turkic, a chunky, tall-lowercase body whose open-mouthed curves stay clear, and that is where the pair is strongest.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-osage: Noto Sans Osage fills the line with lowercase bowls like inflated shapes, and its sweeping curves never close up. And Redux, restful with modest swings in stroke weight, gives that roundness a wide-spaced heading to lean on.
